Subject: Private deploy activation — EU/APAC constraints and failover expectations

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the overview last week. We are finalizing internal approvals to move forward with a Private (VPC) deployment across our EU and APAC footprints. Before procurement signs the SOW we need two concrete items from Redwood:

1) A concise activation criteria checklist for each region (networking, KMS key residency, audit log retention, routing policy) we can attach to our procurement workbook.
2) A clear description of the automated failover behavior between EU and APAC private clusters (how state is handled, expected RTO/RPO, canary/traffic split during failover).

Also copying Jade — they will provide routing peering and network acceptance.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can guarantee that customer data (logs, KV cache, artifacts) for EU tenants remain in EU storage except for transient in-memory replication? We need that for our legal team.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Private deploy activation — EU/APAC constraints and failover expectations

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik and Vivek to validate the ops/network details. High level answers up front:

- Activation checklist: we will produce a 1-page activation criteria per region and a single combined network diagram. That will include required CIDR ranges, BGP/MPLS peering expectations, mandatory firewall rules, TLS requirements, and KMS bindings.
- Data residency guarantee: for Private we can commit to persistent customer-owned storage (S3-compatible or on-prem volume) in the customer-selected region. Audit logs and long-lived artifacts will be written to region-bound storage. We do replicate ephemeral KV caches in-memory across nodes for performance; those are not persisted to a cross-region durable store unless you opt into cross-region replication.
- Failover behavior: default is active-passive with read-only warm standby in the secondary region. We can configure active-active with eventual consistency but that requires additional networking/KMS configuration and has implications for RPO. We will include expected RTO/RPO ranges for both modes in the checklist.

Next steps I propose: Karthik and I will draft the activation checklist and the network diagram and share by EOD Friday. Vivek can outline the SLA exception language and the SRE-runbook excerpt for the failover. Marissa — procurement needs the wording for a SOW addendum for the data residency/KMS clause; can you prepare a draft?

Irene

Alex / team — quick technical detail from networking side. See inline answers and the attached diagram.

> Can you confirm whether Redwood can guarantee that customer data (logs, KV cache, artifacts) for EU tenants remain in EU storage except for transient in-memory replication?

Yes — persistent objects (logs, model artifacts, backups) will be written to EU-bound storage endpoints (we will provide signed endpoints or support your on-prem object storage). Ephemeral KV cache will be in-memory and may be warm-replicated to a standby within the same physical region (AZ-to-AZ inside EU) but not to APAC by default. Cross-region replication is opt-in.

> Failover behavior — how is state handled, expected RTO/RPO, canary/traffic split

Plan options (summary):
- Active-passive (recommended):
  * Standby cluster in APAC is warmed with synced model binaries and configs.
  * KV cache is rebuilt on failover from durable artifacts; expected RTO 8–20 minutes depending on model size and cache warmup; RPO ~= last durable snapshot (minutes).
  * Traffic shift via regional routing policy (we hand off to your load balancer + Jade peering).
- Active-active (advanced):
  * Requires cross-region KMS key replication and a strong consistency layer (adds cost).
  * Typical RTO <2 minutes, RPO near-zero for metadata if properly configured; risk of split-brain if network partition occurs.

Operational requirements we need from Acme / Jade: BGP path preferences for controlled failover, IP allowlists for control plane, and a reachable monitoring webhook for our canary healthchecks. I've attached a refined network diagram and a checklist with the minimum CIDR blocks and peering PSKs.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick tech call to walk Jade through the BGP tiebreak configuration.

—Karthik
